story_spine: A room built out of salt bricks was named one of a design festival's eight best, by a record that could keep what its materials meant but not what they were like.
opening_object_or_event: The five days of a festival on a Bali beach, and a written list of eight pavilions.
reader_initial_state: That a festival happened on a shoreline, and that an account of it named eight pavilions.

beats.happens: A five-day festival occupies a stretch of shoreline in Sanur, and an account of it puts forward eight pavilions as the ones worth attention.
beats.concrete_carrier: the beach at Pengembak, and the written list of eight
beats.must_not_say_yet: Nothing about what the eight descriptions do and do not report; no materials, no sand, no salt taste, no designer aim.

beats.happens: One of the eight, the Oaken Tiltroom, stands as a structure of Himalayan salt brick set partly into the ground, holding fragrances and botanical drinks, made by a Jakarta practice for a contemplative environment shaped by landscape and sensory design, with a stated aim of engaging all the senses.
beats.must_not_say_yet: That none of the eight descriptions reports any visitor's perception; the salt's taste; the sand and its stated meaning.

beats.happens: Another of the pavilions is built so that air moves through a perforated timber facade, trees come up through the roof, and natural rocks serve as places to sit.
beats.concrete_carrier: rocks used as seating under trees that pass through the roof
beats.must_not_say_yet: That none of the eight descriptions reports what any visitor perceived; the closing return to the salt.

beats.happens: In a further pavilion, water comes down rain chains onto ground of sand, and the sand is presented as embodying both strength and fragility.
beats.concrete_carrier: sand underfoot, with water running off the rain chains into it
beats.must_not_say_yet: The general observation about the account's descriptions; the salt's taste against the account's word for it.

beats.happens: Across all eight descriptions the account carries what materials were said to mean and never what anyone standing there perceived, so the sand's strength and fragility is the whole of what is on the record; and the salt of the first pavilion remains a surface with a taste against the word the account gives it.
beats.concrete_carrier: the salt-brick surface itself, and the word 'brick' printed beside it

crip_turn: The sand's description is re-read as the record's own limit: it carries what a material was said to mean rather than what it was to stand on, and what it carried is what anyone downstream can weigh.
ending_move: Close on the salt as a surface with a taste, set against the word the account uses for it.

propositions.proposition: The account describes the sand by what it embodied, not by what it was like underfoot.
Across all eight descriptions, none reports what any visitor perceived.
A record decides what kind of perceiving it can carry, and what it carried is what anyone downstream can weigh.
propositions.prose_realization: IMPLICIT — carried by the sand contrast and the salt callback

propositions.proposition: The salt room is on the list of the most interesting, described by the part of itself that could be written down.
propositions.adds: the specific outcome for this pavilion: it is present in the record by its mineral and absent by its content

propositions.proposition: The salt was a surface someone could have put a tongue to; the account has it as brick.
propositions.returns_to: the salt-brick walls from the opening

_order_rationale: The reader needs a place and a frame before any material can register, so the shoreline and the account's eight come first and establish that everything following arrives through a written selection. The Oaken Tiltroom then arrives at full sensory density, which is the strongest source of the one pressure the article depends on: the reader begins to want the inside of it, and that want must not be satisfied yet. The two intervening pavilions hold that pressure without deflating it, moving from a structure the reader can see through to ground the reader would have to stand on, so the sand lands as the most bodily fact in the piece and the wish to know what it was underfoot is at its sharpest. Only then does the observation about the account's descriptions do any work: it converts the sand from a sensation withheld into a limit of the record, retroactively, without having to be argued. Closing on the salt returns to the densest material the reader already holds, so the last thing they weigh is a surface with a taste against the word the account chose for it.
